pr_title: Disable fast path serialization for types with properties using custom converters.
pr_body:
Disables fast path serialization for types with properties using custom converters. While technically it should be possible to support fast path serialization for this scenario, it would require making the `JsonPropertyInfo.ConverterBase` property public. We should consider doing this in .NET 7.

Fixes #58119.

Milestone: 6.0.0

> While technically it should be possible to support fast path serialization for this scenario, it would require making the JsonPropertyInfo.ConverterBase property public

Why is this? I assume we just need to call `myconverter.Write(`.

>>While technically it should be possible to support fast path serialization for this scenario, it would require making the JsonPropertyInfo.ConverterBase property public
>
>Why is this? I assume we just need to call myconverter.Write(.

property-level converters need to be instantiated and cached with property-level metadata (otherwise we would have to allocate a new converter on each serialization). We currently do cache a `JsonPropertyInfo[]`, however the converter property in `JsonPropertyInfo` has not been made public yet (and therefore cannot be consumed by the fast path serializer). If we wanted to get this working without adding new APIs we would probably need to create a separate `JsonConverter[]` but that would come at the cost of added allocations and redundant code.

The long-term and more ideal implementation is to use the property-level converter in the fast-path, meaning add the new serializer-gen interop API (it will need to be `public`, but treated as `internal`). If we are going to add any other new interop APIs then I think we should use the converter in the fast path, otherwise I think the PR here is fine.

issue_context.title: System.Text.Json code generator: custom converter ignored?
issue_context.body:
I have a class that contains the following property (notice the presence of a custom converter):

```csharp
[JsonPropertyName("tls")]
[JsonConverter(typeof(IntegerBooleanConverter))]
public bool Tls { get; set; }
```

The following snippet gets generated:
```csharp
writer.WriteBoolean(tlsPropName, value.Tls);
```

Correct me if I'm wrong but this seems to ignore my custom converter. I was expecting something along the lines of:
```csharp
writer.WritePropertyName(tlsPropName);
global::System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, value.Tls, global::MyLibrary.Utilities.MyJsonSerializerContext.Default.Tls);
```

Issue Details
I have a class that contains the following property (notice the presence of a custom converter): ```csharp [JsonPropertyName("tls")] [JsonConverter(typeof(IntegerBooleanConverter))] public bool Tls { get; set; } ``` The following snippet gets generated: ```csharp writer.WriteBoolean(tlsPropName, value.Tls); ``` Correct me if I'm wrong but this seems to ignore my custom converter. I was expecting something along the lines of: ```csharp writer.WritePropertyName(tlsPropName); global::System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(writer, value.Tls, global::MyLibrary.Utilities.MyJsonSerializerContext.Default.Tls); ```
Author: Jericho
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Text.Json`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -
Also, note that the issue can be worked around by attaching the JsonConverter attribute to the class definition rather than the property.
Please note that the workaround you suggested does not work for the scenario I presented. I cannot change the `bool` class definition.

We shouldn't need to change defaults.  Here's my understanding of how things should work.
1. If a type can't be supported through fast path deserialization based on information available at compile time we should tell the user and they can make the change.  We should not generate serialization logic that ignores part of the serialization contract.
2. If a type can't be supported through fast path deserialization based on information available at runtime (EG: converter added at runtime), we should fallback to using metadata if present.
